stories.notes: Story has empty acceptance criteria, null spec, and spans three brands (GO, UP, MX) — requires full elaboration of AC, technical depth around live preview architecture, and subsequent hardening for testability, security (preview endpoint auth, XSS in rendered preview), and edge cases (draft vs published state, brand-specific rendering differences). Both agents assigned; openspec first, then speckit reviews.

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability — live preview does not exist yet. Attachment point is useContent (236+ consumers) and the Contentstack SDK service. VCs derived from description since ACs are empty. All VCs stop at the Contentstack boundary (mocked) per unreachable-service constraint. Previous rejection was for missing verificationCriteria — this output includes six VCs covering each named behaviour from the description.

Merged all 8 ACs from openspec's two child stories into a single flat list for the unsplit story, since splitting is openspec's decision alone. Added 6 new criteria: (1) security — preview mode must not activate accidentally in production; (2) edge case — reconnection behavior after connection drop; (3) edge case — null/undefined/empty content after an update; (4) edge case — rapid successive updates (debounce/race condition); (5) error handling — invalid or expired preview token; (6) accessibility — ARIA live-region announcements for screen readers. Did not modify any of openspec's original 8 ACs as they are already observable outcomes with no what-not-how violations. Flagged AC1 for vagueness around 'preview mode' definition. Could not review actual file contents (not provided); criteria are derived from the story description, title, and file paths alone.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents added clear, non-overlapping value: openspec derived 8 ACs from an empty story and split into two logical children (SDK integration → component verification), while speckit hardened with 6 new criteria covering security, edge cases, and accessibility. However, a structural ambiguity exists: the parent story's AC says 'Delegated to split children: AMSD-2041-1, AMSD-2041-2' yet speckit merged all 8 openspec ACs plus 6 new criteria into a flat list on the unsplit parent. It is unclear where speckit's 6 additions (preview-mode safety, reconnection, null content, debounce, expired token, ARIA) actually reside — on the parent or distributed to children. This ownership ambiguity must be resolved by a human before implementation. Additionally, speckit self-flagged AC1 vagueness around 'preview mode' definition, and speckit could not review actual file contents (only description/title/paths), limiting its gap analysis depth.
